review.assessment: The task requires making Counter.increment() thread-safe so concurrent increments are never lost, while keeping the public interface unchanged. This diff creates solution.py with no synchronization primitive whatsoever — there is no lock, mutex, or atomic operation added anywhere. The time.sleep(0) call yields execution between the read and write, which widens rather than closes the race window. Only one acceptance test ran (1 pass), suggesting a lightweight or single-threaded test that cannot expose the concurrency issue.

findings.actual: Lost updates due to non-atomic read-modify-write with no lock
findings.defect: increment is not thread-safe; concurrent calls lose updates because the read (tmp = self.value) and write (self.value = tmp + 1) are separated with no synchronization. The time.sleep(0) yields between them, making interleaving more likely.
findings.expected: The printed value should equal the total number of increment calls across all threads (500 × 10 = 5000). With proper locking, every call is serialized and no updates are lost.
